headline: Computational frameworks couple perturbation screens to single-cell multimodal readouts
label: Perturbation Single Cell Omics Tools
summary: Optical pooled and multimodal single-cell chemical screens now generate terabyte-scale, multi-readout data that require scalable analysis.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational infrastructure for perturbation screens read out at single-cell resolution. SCALLOPS and Brieflow address processing and end-to-end analysis of optical pooled screen images, while icCITE-plex and DOGMA-plex profile RNA, protein, and chromatin responses to chemical perturbations, with MoCAVI and PERCISTRA introduced as accompanying methods. PerturbPair combines Perturb-seq with optical pooled screens in macrophages, and its EB-MoCAVI model imputes and denoises the joint data. What is new is treating perturbation readouts jointly across transcriptomic, protein, chromatin, and imaging modalities rather than any single assay. Adjacent items address lineage tracing (MiTo; CARLIN versus DNA Typewriter), trajectory inference (ATLAS), and evaluation of LLM-based perturbation reasoning and genomic interpretability (CORE, gRely, and the TF-binding benchmark).
